title: Claude Code runs 161 Codex sessions to render frames for a 63-second animated video
summary: Asked to recreate a 63-second animated video, Claude Code launched 161 Codex image-generation sessions and stitched the frames together, the poster says, without describing the finished quality.
agent_role: Claude Code made the plan, launched and supervised 161 Codex sessions, handled memory and failures, and stitched the frames together. The human only gave the initial request.
outcome: Author reports Claude Code orchestrated 161 Codex sessions to produce the video frames; no final quality details are given.
what_they_did: The poster asked Claude Code to recreate a 63-second video in a specific animation style. Claude Code noticed Codex was installed on the machine and decided to use Codex's built-in image generator. It launched 161 Codex sessions to generate frames while it managed RAM, handled failures and stitched the results back together.
how_it_went: The author shares the plan and says Claude orchestrated the whole job. The post does not describe the quality of the finished video.
worth_knowing: Running 161 parallel sessions puts heavy demands on local memory, and the agent had to manage RAM itself. Expect large compute and usage costs.
prompt: Recreate the video at [video file path] in the animation style of [style description or reference images]. Check which tools I have installed, including any image generators, and propose a plan: how many frames, how you will generate them, how you will run work in parallel without exhausting RAM, and how you will retry failures and assemble the final video. Show me the plan and an estimated cost before you start any generation, and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: A novel case of one agent orchestrating another: Claude Code found Codex installed and ran 161 Codex sessions to generate animation frames. The post is a short author's account with no output shown in the text and few reproducible details.
